opening.text: Before a big meal, someone clears the table. The clutter goes. The space opens up. Only then is there room for what matters. Fasting works like that. For a short time we set food aside. The space we make is for prayer, for listening, and for others.

mainMessage.text: Fasting clears the table. It makes room for God and for people who need help.

blocks.text: **A simple commandment** God asked us to fast. It is a small thing that He promised to bless.

Is not this the fast that I have chosen? to loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, and to let the oppressed go free, and that ye break every yoke? Is it not to deal thy bread to the hungry, and that thou bring the poor that are cast out to thy house? when thou seest the naked, that thou cover him; and that thou hide not thyself from thine own flesh?
President Henry B. Eyring, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Is Not This the Fast That I Have Chosen?” from the April 2015 general conference.
So the Lord has given us a simple commandment with a marvelous promise.
Simple, with a promise.
**More than a meal** Giving a fast offering feeds someone. But the Lord's promise goes further than that.

Then shall thy light break forth as the morning, and thine health shall spring forth speedily: and thy righteousness shall go before thee; the glory of the Lord shall be thy rearward. Then shalt thou call, and the Lord shall answer; thou shalt cry, and he shall say, Here I am. If thou take away from the midst of thee the yoke, the putting forth of the finger, and speaking vanity;
President Henry B. Eyring, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Is Not This the Fast That I Have Chosen?” from the April 2015 general conference.
Your fast offering will do more than help feed and clothe bodies. It will heal and change hearts.
It changes hearts.
**Our own responsibility** Caring for those in need is not someone else's job. It is ours.

And now, for the sake of these things which I have spoken unto you—that is, for the sake of retaining a remission of your sins from day to day, that ye may walk guiltless before God—I would that ye should impart of your substance to the poor, every man according to that which he hath, such as feeding the hungry, clothing the naked, visiting the sick and administering to their relief, both spiritually and temporally, according to their wants.

Bishop Dean M. Davies, Second Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric, said this in his talk “The Law of the Fast: A Personal Responsibility to Care for the Poor and Needy” from the October 2014 general conference.
As followers of the Savior, we have a personal responsibility to care for the poor and needy.
It starts with each of us.
**Fasting with a purpose** Fasting is stronger when we pray for something. We can ask the Lord to show us what to do.

And it came to pass that they journeyed many days in the wilderness, and they fasted much and prayed much that the Lord would grant unto them a portion of his Spirit to go with them, and abide with them, that they might be an instrument in the hands of God to bring, if it were possible, their brethren, the Lamanites, to the knowledge of the truth, to the knowledge of the baseness of the traditions of their fathers, which were not correct.
President Henry B. Eyring, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Is Not This the Fast That I Have Chosen?” from the April 2015 general conference.
The Lord’s servants will pray and fast for the revelation to know whom to help and what help to give.
Fast and ask.
**Caring is gospel doctrine** Helping the poor is not an extra. It is at the heart of the gospel. When we help them, we serve the Savior.
And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.

Bishop Dean M. Davies, Second Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric, said this in his talk “The Law of the Fast: A Personal Responsibility to Care for the Poor and Needy” from the October 2014 general conference.
Caring for the poor and needy is a fundamental gospel doctrine and an essential element in the eternal plan of salvation.
We serve Him as we serve them.
**The promise of a watered garden** Isaiah said the Lord would guide us and satisfy our souls. The blessings are real and many.
And the Lord shall guide thee continually, and satisfy thy soul in drought, and make fat thy bones: and thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not.
President Henry B. Eyring, First Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Is Not This the Fast That I Have Chosen?” from the April 2015 general conference.
The commandment to fast for the poor has many blessings attached to it.
The blessings are many.

story.title: Jesus Christ fasts in the wilderness

blocks.text: Before His ministry began, the Savior went alone into the wilderness.
Then was Jesus led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted of the devil. And when he had fasted forty days and forty nights, he was afterward an hungred.
Jesus Christ fasted to prepare for hard things. He shows us that fasting is a way to draw near to God before the work begins.

application.text: First, choose a purpose for your next fast. Second, begin with a prayer and end with a prayer. Third, pay a fast offering, and give as generously as you can.

story.title: Fasting for the souls of others

blocks.text: The Nephite church was growing. The people gathered often to fast and pray.
Nevertheless the children of God were commanded that they should gather themselves together oft, and join in fasting and mighty prayer in behalf of the welfare of the souls of those who knew not God.
They fasted for people they hadn't even met. Fasting can carry love beyond our own home.

application.text: First, ask God who needs your prayers this month. Second, fast and pray for that person. Third, do one small thing for them.

story.title: The people of Nineveh fast

blocks.text: Jonah warned a great city that it would be destroyed. The people took his words to heart.

So the people of Nineveh believed God, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them even to the least of them. For word came unto the king of Nineveh, and he arose from his throne, and he laid his robe from him, and covered him with sackcloth, and sat in ashes. And he caused it to be proclaimed and published through Nineveh by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying, Let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste any thing: let them not feed, nor drink water:
From the king to the least of them, the whole city humbled itself. Fasting can be done together, and it can turn a whole people toward God.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they fasted and prayed for someone who was ill or struggling. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Fasting for Alma

blocks.text: Alma the Younger had been struck down and could not speak. The priests and his father fasted and prayed for him.

And he caused that the priests should assemble themselves together; and they began to fast, and to pray to the Lord their God that he would open the mouth of Alma, that he might speak, and also that his limbs might receive their strength—that the eyes of the people might be opened to see and know of the goodness and glory of God. And it came to pass after they had fasted and prayed for the space of two days and two nights, the limbs of Alma received their strength, and he stood up and began to speak unto them, bidding them to be of good comfort:

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they gave themselves to faithful service, including fasting. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Anna serves with fasting

blocks.text: Anna was a widow of great age. She spent her days at the temple.

And there was one Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Aser: she was of a great age, and had lived with an husband seven years from her virginity; And she was a widow of about fourscore and four years, which departed not from the temple, but served God with fastings and prayers night and day.
Anna fasted and prayed for many years. She was one of the first to recognize the baby Jesus Christ as the Redeemer. Faithful fasting prepares us to see Him.
